key_insight: Decoupling radar-state prediction from language alignment improves radar-to-text retrieval without degrading continuous physical-state estimates.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports privacy-preserving motion and scene monitoring under darkness, clutter, sensor blackouts, and through-wall conditions, rather than directly modeling material fracture.
method: Combine a clock anchor and dual-scale RF encoder with an LLM adapted using approximately 3% LoRA parameters.
Train denoising and rollout with EMA-JEPA and Batch-VICReg to predict physical states 3 seconds ahead.
Freeze the physical backbone and train a separate language-alignment head with stop-gradient and false-negative masking.
evidence_signal: On 4,541 radar windows across three domains and against 10 baselines, the decoupled head raised retrieval R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% while preserving physical readouts, including 3.37° blackout torso-tilt error at +3 seconds.
watch_item: Retrieval R@10 remains 15.01%, and the reported radar benchmarks do not establish performance for solid-mechanics damage or fracture monitoring.
paper_title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
